# RepoHunter

> RepoHunter checks a GitHub repo before you or your AI agent adopt it. It returns GO, MAYBE or SKIP with the reasons: whether the repo is maintained or archived, what its license allows (including resale), a heuristic safety scan of its text and agent config files, and whether it runs on your machine. It runs locally as an MCP server, a Claude Code plugin, and a CLI. Python standard library only, MIT licensed.

When to use it: before adding a dependency, cloning a tool, or installing a skill or MCP server. Agents should call `evaluate_repo` on a candidate before installing it and treat the verdict as guidance, not a guarantee.

## Install

- Claude Code (MCP server): `claude mcp add repohunter -- uvx --from git+https://github.com/meetziggy/repohunter repohunter-mcp`
- Claude Code (plugin: server plus the skill that tells the agent when to use it): `/plugin marketplace add meetziggy/repohunter` then `/plugin install repohunter`
- Codex: `codex mcp add repohunter -- uvx --from git+https://github.com/meetziggy/repohunter repohunter-mcp`
- Any MCP client (Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Zed, Cline): stdio server, command `uvx`, args `["--from", "git+https://github.com/meetziggy/repohunter", "repohunter-mcp"]`
- CLI, no install: `uvx --from git+https://github.com/meetziggy/repohunter repohunter scan owner/repo`

Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Not yet published on PyPI. An optional `GITHUB_TOKEN` raises rate limits; it stays on the user's machine.

## MCP tools

- `evaluate_repo(repo, project?)`: should I reuse this repo? Real GitHub stats, a score breakdown, hardware fit, and a GO / MAYBE / SKIP verdict. Pass `project` for a relevance read.
- `find_repos(query)`: reuse candidates for a need, from live GitHub search, ranked.
- `portfolio_scan(user)`: facts-only summary of a GitHub user's or org's public work.

Results carry an `evidence` block (sources, method, limits) and mark repo-authored text as untrusted. The safety scan runs in the CLI (`repohunter scan owner/repo`).

## Limits

- Scores are a transparent heuristic over public GitHub data: guidance, not a guarantee, and not a security audit.
- The safety scan is heuristic: a clean result means these checks found nothing, not that a repo is safe.
- The license read states facts and a call; it is not legal advice.
